stories.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.

George Russell closed the gap in the drivers' championship to 66 points from his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli after taking his third win of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Antonelli, who was hampered with all sorts of issues across the weekend, recovered from P16 to finish fifth.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the next race.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- George Russell warns 'pressure' is on Kimi Antonelli after 'most dominant weekend in my career'

- Lando Norris: Drivers should have 'one-race ban' after collision with Franco Colapinto at Azerbaijan GP

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 2

Practice One: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Saturday, October 3

Final Practice: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Sunday, October 4

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: 8 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the Bahrain GP being hosted in Malaysia?
The Bahrain Grand Prix was cancelled in April due to the war in Iran, but it has now been rescheduled and will now be staged in Malaysia, meaning the race will remain on the F1 calendar.

There were several reasons why Malaysia was an obvious alternative, the main one being the way the calendar fell and the logistics involved.

It sits between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took place at the weekend, and will be followed by the Singapore Grand Prix on Oct. 11, resulting in a triple-header.

The last time the Malaysia Grand Prix held a race was in 2017. It spent 18 years on the calendar, so the infrastructure is there to be able to host a race with not much notice.

Sepang International Circuit

The Sepang is one of the circuits that is a complete test of car performance and driver ability. There is a mixture of long straights, heavy-braking zones and fast, flowing corners.

It is always one of the most humid races and due to the tropical weather, there can be heavy downpours of rain, changing the course of a race in an instant.

The combination of weather and the characteristics of the circuit always provide an exciting race and it is a driver and fan favourite as a result.

There is a tight hairpin at Turn 15, but either side are long straights which provide excellent overtaking opportunities.

Previous winners in Malaysia

2010: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2011: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2012: Fernando Alonso (Ferrari)

2013: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1999

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Lap record: 1:34.080 Sebastian Vettel (2017).

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel with four victories (2010-2011, 2013 and 2015). From the current grid, Fernando Alonso with three (2005, 2007 and 2012), Lewis Hamilton (2014), and Max Verstappen (2017) have each won here.

Most poles: Michael Schumacher (1999, 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2004) and Lewis Hamilton with five (2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017). From the current grid, Alonso has two poles (2003, 2005).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia is thundery showers and light winds through the weekend with highs of 33°C.

What happened in 2017?
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race in dominant fashion after qualifying third on the grid. It was Lewis Hamilton's race to lose after he put his Mercedes on pole for the race which he's won once before, but he crossed the line in second.

Verstappen's teammate Daniel Ricciardo finished third, while Sebastian Vettel, who started from the back of the grid after suffering engine problems at Ferrari, managed to recover positions on the grid to finish fourth overall.

Vettel was 34 points behind Hamilton in the drivers' championship with five races to go.

Who will win this year?

There will be a slight element of the unknown heading into Malaysia given that over half of the grid have never raced here before. Teams and drivers have historic data to go off, but nobody will really know how the cars will perform until Friday's practice.

Russell didn't put a foot wrong last time out at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and was incredibly quick all weekend and will carry that momentum into the next round.

Mercedes are also due to bring a major upgrade to Malaysia, while McLaren are expected to be strong around the high-speed circuit.

Red Bull brought major upgrades to Baku and were well in the fight, so rival teams will be keeping a close eye on Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

With rain expected, and it being one of the most popular circuits in F1, it could be an absolute thriller.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu (Manchester United)

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Denmark head coach Brian Riemer told broadcaster TV2 after the game: "He has an injury and has to go home."

Cody Gakpo (Liverpool)

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

Noussair Mazraoui (Manchester United)

The United full-back was forced out of Morocco's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Lesotho after 69 minutes. He was holding his back while on the floor after a challenge.

Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City)

O'Reilly missed England's win against Czechia on Tuesday night after also missing training on Monday. Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha was called into the matchday squad.

Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham Hotspur)

The Tottenham defender Jan Paul van Hecke picked up a foot injury in the Netherlands' clash with Serbia and withdrew from the Netherlands' squad during a training session.

No replacement will be called up for van Hecke. He is now returning to Spurs.

International breaks this season

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Oct. 1

Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Red Sox's Sonny Gray not happy for being lifted after 70 pitches
stories.summary: Red Sox ace Sonny Gray said after Wednesday's loss to the Yankees that he was frustrated for being lifted after throwing only 70 pitches.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- With the Boston bats ice cold at Yankee Stadium again, a couple of quick hooks by Red Sox rookie manager Chad Tracy led to another early postseason exit.

And top starter Sonny Gray wasn't happy about being lifted after only 70 pitches.

"I think I'm the best pitcher in the American League going through the order a third time. I think that's a fact," Gray said. "I would have liked to have been trusted in that moment."

For the second consecutive season, the Red Sox were sent home for the winter by their biggest rivals as the New York Yankees rolled to a 9-2 victory Wednesday night and a two-game sweep of their wild-card series.

Boston was outscored 18-2 overall and left to lament a miserable finish to this roller-coaster ride of a season that included Tracy taking over when Alex Cora was fired in April.

Tracy's decision-making came under fire after both games against the Yankees. In Boston's 9-0 defeat a night earlier, Tracy pulled starter Payton Tolle after 4⅔ innings and 83 pitches in a 1-0 game.

Last year, the Red Sox won their wild-card series opener before losing to the Yankees in a deciding Game 3 as they got overpowered by Cam Schlittler, who pitched another playoff gem against his hometown team Tuesday night.

"To have it end here two times in a row is tough," shortstop Trevor Story said.

Facing a New York lineup missing injured slugger Aaron Judge, the Red Sox gave up 26 hits despite a pair of effective performances from their starting pitchers.

At the plate, Boston mustered only seven hits and finally snapped a 26-inning postseason scoring drought that dated to last year when Willson Contreras homered just over the right-center fence in the sixth Wednesday.

"It's obviously been an eventful year. In the moment right now you can't think much more other than anything but the fact that we just lost a playoff series," Tracy said.

Needing a victory to extend their season, the Red Sox sent Gray to the mound and the 18-game winner certainly gave them a chance. Boston trailed 1-0 in the fifth when the right-hander allowed a two-out single to Ben Rice that put runners at the corners.

Tracy then yanked Gray, eager to hand the ball to baseball's best bullpen during the regular season.

"I felt good. I felt crisp. I felt sharp. I think I got clipped for a solo home run and then some singles, but I felt like I stayed on the attack throughout," Gray said. "I'm frustrated, for sure. You know, not ready for it to end. A lot of emotions."

Asked about the move to pull Gray, Contreras put his finger over his lips to zip them shut.

"It's not enough when you have talent or you have data or you have computers that's telling you what to do, because this is baseball," he said. "The data is here to help us, but at the end of the day you are going to have to need experience and veteran guys to win games."

In both games of the series, Tracy gave the ball to left-handed reliever Erik Miller after taking out his starting pitchers.

On Tuesday, Rice greeted Miller with a 423-foot solo homer to straightaway center field.

On Wednesday, Tracy summoned Miller to face a different left-handed batter, Cody Bellinger -- who batted .274 against lefties this season and .259 versus right-handers. In fact, his .310 batting average against left-handers over the past two years was the best of any left-handed hitter in the majors.

Bellinger made Tracy and the Red Sox pay, lining an RBI single to right field.

"We're struggling to score runs," Tracy said. "And when you get in spots where you're struggling to score runs and you're already trailing, you feel like you've got to be aggressive and go."

Back from a shoulder injury, ace starter Garrett Crochet entered in the sixth for his first outing since April 25 and first relief appearance since 2023 with the Chicago White Sox. The left-hander opened with a strikeout, but Spencer Jones reached safely on a wild pitch, and Crochet never got an out.

Bellinger's three-run homer off right-hander Garrett Whitlock capped a six-run inning that made it 8-1, and the Red Sox were finished. A bullpen that led the majors with a 3.00 ERA during the regular season finished this series with a 20.25 ERA after giving up 15 runs, 15 hits and seven walks in 6⅔ innings, with a .484 opponents' batting average.

Boston's latest downfall in the Bronx was a crushing end to a wild 2026 season for the Red Sox, who stumbled to a 32-46 start. Tracy was the skipper at Triple-A Worcester before getting promoted to interim manager in Boston, and the team finally began to take off with a four-game sweep of the Yankees at Fenway Park in late June.

After clinching a wild-card spot last week, the Red Sox removed the interim tag and named Tracy the 49th manager in team history, signing him to a three-year contract that runs through the 2029 season, with a club option for 2030. The team also exercised the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.

"I wasn't there for the highs and lows," Crochet said. "For this team to do what it did do, to make it to this point, was nothing short of miraculous."

Led by Gray and Contreras, among others, the Red Sox went on a 15-game winning streak in July that equaled a franchise record and used a 32-5 surge to climb back into contention. They became the fourth team in major league history to reach the postseason after falling 14 games under .500, and the first to qualify after losing as many as 44 of its first 75.

"I'm proud of what we accomplished," Gray said. "We were left for dead there for a while."

stories.headline: Wings' Ogunbowale scores record 45 to force Game 3 vs. Valkyries
stories.summary: Arike Ogunbowale delivered a record-breaking performance with the Wings' season on the line, scoring 45 points, including a tying 3-pointer to force overtime, to help Dallas force a deciding Game 3 against the Valkyries.
stories.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Arike Ogunbowale stood near Paige Bueckers and waited for the star guard to make a move on her dribble with the Dallas Wings trailing by three as the final seconds of regulation -- and their season -- ticked away.

Bueckers waved toward her backcourt mate, but she wasn't telling Ogunbowale to get out of the way. She was telling her to get open.

After all, Bueckers knew whom the hot hand was -- and it wasn't her.

Ogunbowale took a pass from Bueckers on the left baseline, dribbled toward the corner and hit an off-balance corner 3-pointer, sending the game to overtime and her on the way to a WNBA playoff-record 45 points as the Wings won a thriller 108-100 on Wednesday night, forcing a Game 3 in their first-round series.

The deciding game will be Friday night in San Francisco, where the Valkyries won the series opener by 24 points.

Golden State is trying to advance in the playoffs for the first time in the franchise's second season. The Wings are trying to reach the semifinals for the second time in six postseason appearances since moving to the Dallas area in 2016.

Ogunbowale opened the extra period of Game 2 by banking in a 3, then hit another one to put Dallas ahead for good at 103-100 with 1:46 remaining. A four-time All-Star, she easily topped her previous playoff best of 24 points after scoring 10 points on just seven shots in the series opener.

"We felt like we got pushed around out there when we played in San Francisco, and especially me, personally, I don't feel like I was aggressive," Ogunbowale said. "I didn't know what I would score. I was going to shoot regardless because I just feel like seven shots isn't enough to win playoffs and I have to be aggressive whether it's going in or not."

Bueckers, the 2025 No. 1 overall pick and Rookie of the Year who is in her first playoff series, was mired in a 3-for-13 shooting night that included an air ball on a 3-pointer with the Wings trailing by three in the final two minutes of regulation. But she assisted on Ogunbowale's tying 3, and again on a the banked 3 to start OT. Bueckers finished with 10 points and had four assists.

"For us to do what we did today without Paige having the type of game that she always has offensively for us, to come out with a win is huge," Wings coach Jose Fernandez said. "We had other people step up."

Ogunbowale's shot for a 93-93 tie with 4.1 seconds left in regulation of Game 2 was followed by Gabby Williams getting called for an offensive foul on the inbound play after a Golden State timeout.

That call was reversed on replay, so instead of Aziaha James having a chance to give Dallas the lead at the free throw line, there was a jump ball at center court with 3.0 seconds to go. After a scramble for the loose ball, Golden State's desperation shot was way off target and after the buzzer.

Williams scored 36 points, a career-high for regular season or playoffs, but she missed all six of her shots in the final 1:31 of overtime to finish 12-of-23 from the field.

"We got one at home, and we got to bring our best," Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said. "That was not our best. Tomorrow's got to be clear minds, clear focus, clear game plan, and then be ready to go for the game at home."

Ogunbowale scored 22 points in the fourth quarter and overtime -- 11 in each period. She passed her previous overall career high of 41 points with the 3 that put Dallas up for good.

Dallas' Alysha Clark tied her playoff career high with 21 points, and Aziaha James added 13.

Kaila Charles scored 14 points for the Valkyries, and Kayla Thornton had 13.

With the scored tied at 98 in the extra period, Ogunbowale and Tiffany Hayes had to be separated after making contact. Both were called for flagrant fouls, and each made a pair of free throws with 2:26 remaining.

The Valkyries didn't score again, shooting 2-of-12 in overtime.

stories.headline: Sources: Steelers to trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys
stories.summary: The Steelers agreed to trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
After a lengthy and contentious contract standoff and a lingering back issue, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is going to the Dallas Cowboys.

The Steelers on Wednesday night agreed to trade Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources told ESPN.

The trade marks the end of a monthslong saga that stretched throughout the Steelers' offseason as Porter, one of the team's 2023 second-round picks, awaited an extension and was sidelined by a back injury.

The heart of the dispute was the guaranteed money within the contract's structure, sources told ESPN, and the sides never made meaningful progress on agreeing to terms despite talks as late as hours before kickoff of the Steelers' Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers then stopped talks because they don't negotiate during the regular season as a longstanding organizational principle.

Porter, who started 41 games and had three interceptions in three seasons, sat out all of the team's training camp and preseason after reporting an aggravation to the back injury during the team's mobility workout on the first day of camp. He was put on the physically unable to perform list until roster cutdown day in late August.

Porter was then a limited participant in every regular-season practice until earlier this week as coach Mike McCarthy said the cornerback was progressing through a "ramp-up" phase during the first month of the season.

Porter was inactive for each of the first three games and had been ruled out earlier Wednesday of the Steelers' game Thursday night against the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers added a back injury to Wednesday's practice report in addition to the "not injury related-conditioning" description the team used for Porter's injury status for most of the past three weeks. Porter had previously been a full participant in the team's Monday and Tuesday walkthroughs.

His departure means the Steelers will continue to operate with Asante Samuel Jr., Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette rotating at outside cornerback. Everette, a 2026 third-round draft pick, played extended snaps in a Week 3 win against the Cincinnati Bengals, first coming in for a briefly injured Dean and then replacing Samuel for much of the second half.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones hinted during training camp that he would be willing to give up draft capital to help this season's team. Jones was asked on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Monday about a potential trade with reports of the team's interest in Porter.

While not specifically talking about Porter because of tampering rules, Jones said, "I'd just say we're right on top of it. We're very aware of the moving parts out here."

The Cowboys have had a need for cornerback help with Cobie Durant expected to sit out his second game because of a hamstring strain. In last weekend's loss to the Baltimore Ravens, Durant's replacement, Shavon Revel, injured his knee and ankle. He was limited in Wednesday's practice. Revel sat out the first eight games of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL in his right knee sustained while at East Carolina, but the current injury is to his left knee.

At the end of the game against the Ravens, the Cowboys used backups Caelen Carson and Ameer Speed opposite DaRon Bland with Reddy Steward, a practice squad call-up, working the slot.

This is the third trade between the Cowboys and Steelers in the past two years. In May 2025, the Cowboys sent a 2026 third-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder to Pittsburgh for wide receiver George Pickens and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

In August, the Cowboys acquired tackle Broderick Jones and a 2027 fourth-rounder for third- and sixth-round picks in 2027.

The Ringer first reported news of the Porter trade.

stories.headline: MacKinnon has 2 goals and a rare fight in the Avs' 8-4 victory over the Kings in opener
stories.summary: — Nathan MacKinnon scored twice in a four-goal second period and capped his night with a rare fight, and the Colorado Avalanche opened the season with an 8-4 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
DENVER -- — Nathan MacKinnon scored twice in a four-goal second period and capped his night with a rare fight, and the Colorado Avalanche opened the season with an 8-4 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Wednesday night.


Hours before the game, Colorado coach Jared Bednar was given a four-year contract extension. Bednar, who led Colorado to the 2022 Stanley Cup title, was in the final year of his current contract. The extension ended speculation on his future after being swept by Vegas in the Western Conference finals last spring.


“I didn’t want him to go through the whole year and have those distractions of being asked that same question, especially as the year goes on,” Avs president and general manager Joe Sakic said before Wednesday night’s game.


Artturi Lehkonen had two goals, Brock Nelson had a goal and two assist and Mackenzie Blackwood made 26 saves for Colorado, which scored four times on the power play and allowed two short-handed goals.


MacKinnon, who had a career-high 53 goals last season, scored on a 5-on-3 just 23 seconds into the second period and gave the Avs a 4-2 lead with his second at 8:33.


The 2024 MVP, whose last fight was four years ago, dropped the gloves with Kings defenseman Brandt Clark with Colorado leading 6-4 late in the third. Avs captain Gabriel Landeskog scored less than a minute later and Lehkonen iced it with his second 1:03 later.


Trevor Moore, Joel Armia and Brian Dumoulin scored for Los Angeles, and Darcy Kuemper stopped 21 shots.


Nelson and Kelly scored in the first period to give the Avs a 2-1 lead, and Moore and Armia had goals in the second period for the Kings.


Artemi Panarin scored on a delayed penalty midway through the third.


Up next
Kings: At San Jose on Saturday night.


Avalanche: Host St. Louis on Saturday night

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey: 'I want to be judged by winning'
stories.summary: Coming off a career year, Tyrese Maxey said he doesn't want to be judged by how he does individually but by how the 76ers do as a team this year.
stories.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Having earned two All-Star nods in the last three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-high 28.3 points per game, Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey is primed for another big year.

But the 25-year-old said Wednesday after the Sixers' second practice of training camp that the only metric he cares about for Philadelphia's highly anticipated upcoming season is team success.

"I'm at the point now where I've showed what I can do talent-wise," Maxey said. "Of course, I'm going to continue to get better, but I want to be judged by winning. If we win, that's what I want to be judged by. That's really my main mindset, my main goal, is finding ways to win."

Maxey was the first of Philly's four major stars -- including Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James -- to speak to reporters since training camp started Tuesday.

Brown sidestepped a query on media day Monday when asked about how the Sixers will determine a pecking order and identify an "alpha" by replying: "Next question."

Maxey's answer was in the same spirit, albeit much more elaborate, as he detailed his willingness to adjust to help the team.

"Because I've played so many different roles, I'm capable of doing so many different things," Maxey said. "And I think that's going to be a positive for myself and for this team. I can play on the ball. I can play off the ball. I can play in transition. I can catch and shoot. Play off [of] pin downs. I can play pick-and-roll. ...

"I'm going to play however they need me to play. However Coach [Nick Nurse] wants to play, that's how I'm going to play."

And Maxey is not only leading by example. He is speaking up as the new group gets off the ground.

"My voice carries a little bit and then just the charisma of me smiling and having a good time," Maxey said. "I mean, I'm getting older ... and I just feel like I've been here for a minute. Process [Embiid] has been here, I think what, 13 years? I've been here seven. So, we've been here for a while, kind of know how things go around here and just am trying to keep using my voice and help everybody get familiar and help everybody get comfortable."

Beyond vowing to acquiesce to any role change that is asked of him, Maxey also used his voice to be effusive in his praise of the other stars on the team in his answers Wednesday.

On James: "That's like a big brother to me. He's an old man ... He's a good guy. He's a good guy."

On Embiid: "He looks amazing. He looks happy. ... When you're healthy and you're happy and you're at peace with your life and basketball, that's when you're at your best. He's been great."

On Brown: "JB's like physically a freak of nature. He's just stronger than you. He jumps higher than you. He's faster than you and he's very talented. Those are the things that you see every single day. And I think what's stood out to me so far is his communication and he's willing to pick up the ball defensively, kind of just do whatever coach needs him to do right now."

Brown was the last player on the court after practice, working on handling double teams in the post - by kicking out to a shooter or fading away for a jumper along the baseline - with a massive Sixers logo on the wall of the practice facility behind him.

Maxey made sure to acknowledge the transition for Brown, too, as he begins life with the Sixers after having played for the Boston Celtics for his entire career before being traded within the Atlantic Division in July.

"This is very foreign to him, imagine being somewhere for [10] years and coming here, the team that you're trained to hate, probably," Maxey said. "It's been great. Especially [since] we just beat [Boston in the playoffs]. It's kind of crazy."

stories.headline: Roosters star admits he is torn on World Cup decision
stories.summary: Robert Toia has revealed he is still undecided if he wants to play for Australia or Tonga in the World Cup, less than a week out from teams being named.
stories.body:
Robert Toia has admitted he still doesn't know who he wants to play for at the World Cup, as the in-demand centre weighs up representing Tonga or Australia.

Toia is the highest-profile player caught in a tug-of-war between nations, with the World Cup just a fortnight ago and final squads to be announced next week.

Tonga coach Kristian Woolf had told AAP this week that Toia had indicated he wanted to represent the Pacific nation, after debuting for them last year.

Australia counterpart Kevin Walters has also made clear he believes the Sydney Roosters star is available for the Kangaroos, and he has not been told otherwise.

Toia has accepted he must make a decision soon, but remains uncertain what way he will go with Sunday's NRL grand final against Newcastle before this month's tournament.

"To be honest, I have not made my mind up," Toia told AAP.

"I just find it hard that I don't have a decision. I want to play for Tonga, it means so much to my family, myself and my people.

"I went over to Tonga last year and you can see how much it means to them.

"But to have Australia on your resume. Just to play for Australia, in my second year, I find it such a massive achievement. That's what I'm kind of weighing up."

Beyond Toia, Woolf also believes Sydney Roosters teammates Salesi Foketi and Siua Wong want to play for Tonga in the global showpiece.

Queensland winger Jojo Fifita revealed this week he too was still undecided, weighing up whether to play for Australia, New Zealand or Tonga.

Fifita told AAP he'd had discussions with all three nations, although he was not named in the Kiwis' initial 40-man squad.

Walters has said both Jojo and his brother David are under consideration for Australia's World Cup squad.

In better news for Tonga, Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa has confirmed he will be fit for the tournament after a syndesmosis injury in the preliminary-final loss to the Roosters.

"I don't need surgery. I will be able to play in the World Cup," Katoa said.

"I immediately knew I had done something, so I was definitely happy once I got the scans back it wasn't too bad and I will be able to represent Tonga."

Complicating matters for players who are weighing up their future is the fact Australian representatives stand to earn $40,000 by playing in the tournament.

AAP is aware of coaches and players who are concerned that may prompt some players to choose the Kangaroos in order to benefit their families.

But Katoa said it would never be a factor for him.

"I'd never look at the price tag, it's always where my heart is at," he said.

"I've always said my heart is at Tonga and if it wasn't for Tonga I am half-Cook Islands as well. So if it wasn't for Tonga, I would go Cook Islands."

Meanwhile it is understood Tonga will pick former St George Illawarra half Talatau Amone in their squad for the tournament.

Amone has not played since he was deregistered by the NRL in 2023 for assault. Tonga are still yet to learn if he will be cleared to play in the tournament.

He can return to the NRL next year, and starred on his return to Queensland Cup with Wynnum-Manly in recent months.

stories.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?
stories.summary: Formula 1 is heading to Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix; the south-east Asian nation providing an unusual setting for a race.
stories.body:
Formula 1 is heading to Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix; the south-east Asian nation providing an unusual setting for a race that should have taken place a) back in April and b) over 4,000 miles away.

The sport last raced at the Sepang International Circuit in 2017 -- meaning more than half of the grid are set to take it on for the first time. Some, meanwhile, weren't even teenagers on the day Max Verstappen triumphed ahead of Lewis Hamilton and Daniel Ricciardo.

Ahead of this weekend's race, ESPN has rounded up what all 22 drivers were doing at the time of that last Malaysian GP.

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

Lewis Hamilton
At the time, Hamilton was a three-time world champion, having won his first title with McLaren in 2008 before adding two more with Mercedes in 2014 and 2015. He would win a fourth in 2017 -- and returns to Malaysia nine years later with seven titles to his name.

During the race nine years ago he finished second to Verstappen, who was in his second season at Red Bull at the time.

Hamilton shares the record for most poles at Sepang with Michael Schumacher, with five each, and he was the last driver on the current grid to take pole here.

Charles Leclerc
The Monégasque was racing in Formula 2 with Prema Racing and was the runaway leader at the time.

Leclerc did, however, get a taste of an F1 weekend as -- not for the first time -- he competed in FP1 in place of Marcus Ericsson. He was three-tenths quicker than Pascal Wehrlein.

Leclerc went on to win the F2 drivers' championship that same year, earning himself a spot in the highest tier of motorsport a year later as a full-time F1 driver for Sauber.

Kimi Antonelli
The Mercedes driver, who is currently leading the drivers' championship and is on course to be the youngest to hold the title, has never raced in Malaysia. He was karting in Europe at the time and was only 11 years old.

Antonelli, now 20, is 66 points ahead of teammate George Russell and has eight career victories in what is only his second season in F1.

George Russell
In 2017, the Englishman was racing in GP3 with ART Grand Prix and went on to win the championship that year in his rookie season.

He later made his F1 debut for Williams in 2019, so missed out on racing in Malaysia by two years.

Fernando Alonso
Alonso, who is now the oldest driver on the grid at 45 years old, was racing for McLaren-Honda in 2017.

At the time he was driving an uncompetitive car and finished the season 15th in the title standings, scoring points in only five races.

In Malaysia, he finished outside the points in 11th.

Lance Stroll
The Canadian has been in F1 for longer than most on the grid and was racing for Williams at the time. He finished eighth and picked up four points in what was his rookie season.

Alex Albon
Albon was regularly racing against Leclerc in F2 for ART Grand Prix in 2017. He finished his rookie season in 10th and two years later he made his F1 debut for Toro Rosso.

After a stint at Red Bull and a year as its reserve driver, he then signed for Williams in 2022 and has been there for the last five seasons. He joins the majority of the grid in racing in Malaysia for the first time.

Carlos Sainz

The Spaniard is one of the drivers who has raced here before when he was driving for Toro Rosso.

But it didn't last for long as he only completed half the race after suffering a power unit issue, which forced him to retire from seventh place.

Lando Norris

Norris was another driver who was racing -- and winning a title -- in a junior series, clinching the European Formula 3 championship with Carlin.

During the same year he joined McLaren's Driver Development Programme, before making his F1 debut in 2019 with the team.

Oscar Piastri

The Australian was competing in the F4 British Championship and ended up finishing the season second. He was racing for TRS Arden Junior Racing Team.

Esteban Ocon
Ocon, soon to be an F1 free agent, was racing for Force India at the last race here in 2017 and finished with a point in 10th.

Oliver Bearman
The young Briton was still karting in the UK. In 2017, he won the Kartmasters British Grand Prix in the Honda Cadet category at the age of 12

Max Verstappen

F1's four-time world champion was competing in his first full season for Red Bull after getting promoted early into 2016 after just one year under his belt at Toro Rosso.

He was only 20 years old at the time of the last race in Malaysia, but he won from third place after a dominant drive.

Verstappen passed Hamilton on Lap 4 and he was in control of the race from there.

Isack Hadjar

Hadjar joins the list as one of the youngsters who has never raced here. He was 13 years old at the time and was karting in France before progressing to the international scene.

Liam Lawson
New Zealander Lawson was competing in Australia in the Formula 4 Championship and ended up finishing second with his team BRM at the age of 15.

Arvid Lindblad

In 2017, Arvid Lindblad was competing in British karting championships, specifically racing in the cadet categories IAME Cadet and Honda Cadet.

Lindblad is the youngest driver on the current grid and was only nine at the time of the last Malaysian GP.

Franco Colapinto

Colapinto was competing at a high level in karting and won the Argentine Pre-Junior Karting Championship the year before.

In 2017, he won the Buenos Aires Regional Championship in the junior class, before moving to the UK to continue his racing career.

Pierre Gasly

Gasly made his Formula 1 debut at the 2017 Malaysian Grand Prix, replacing Daniil Kvyat at Toro Rosso, and finished 14th.

Nico Hülkenberg

Hülkenberg was racing for Renault and finished down in 16th. The German driver had previously been at Force India.

Gabriel Bortoleto

Bortoleto was racing for CRG Factory Team in the OK Junior karting category in Europe after making the move from Brazil. He was 12 at the time.

He became a full-time F1 driver with Sauber in 2025, ahead of the team's transition to Audi.

Sergio Pérez

The Mexican driver has raced in Malaysia seven times during his F1 career. In 2017, he was racing for Force India and finished the race in sixth.

Valtteri Bottas

Bottas was Hamilton's Mercedes teammate and started fifth on the grid, finishing in the same position.

stories.headline: Premier League depth charts for most popular teams: Who is key?
stories.summary: The Premier League is well underway, but with the transfer window closed, where do players stand in their teams? How deep do the squads go?
stories.body:
The Premier League season is five games in, and with the transfer window closed until Jan. 1, there will be no more incomings or outgoings (unless a free agent can be snapped up.)

As teams start to hit their stride and summer additions become accustomed to their surroundings, it's time to take a look at where the players stand with their respective squads.

Here are depth charts of the best options for the first XI and backup XI for the six most-followed clubs in the league. Of course, it's hard to predict who could be called upon as the fixtures pile up, but this should give you an idea of how strong each team is.

(Note: Each player appears in the main squad list once, even if he could fit into multiple spots. We have also included injured players, although those likely to be out for the season are noted separately.)

ARSENAL

Goalkeeper: David Raya, Kepa Arrizabalaga, Illan Meslier

Right back: Jurriën Timber, Ben White

Left back: Riccardo Calafiori, Piero Hincapié,

Center back: William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhães, Cristhian Mosquera, Ezri Konsa

Central midfield: Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi, Bruno Guimarães, Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly

Attacking midfield/Forward: Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Eberechi Eze, Martin Ødegaard,

Striker: Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyökeres

FIRST XI (4-2-3-1)

Raya

Timber, Saliba, Gabriel Magalhães, Calafiori

Rice, Guimarães

Saka, Ødegaard, Tzolis

Havertz

SECOND XI (4-3-3)

Kepa

White, Konsa, Mosquera, Hincapié

Lewis-Skelly, Merino

Madueke, Eze, Dowman

Gyökeres

EXTRAS: Meslier, Zubimendi

Arsenal came out of the summer window having executed their plans well. Those who departed were moved out largely on the club's terms, while the arrivals were clearly targeted according to specific requirements. The only slightly ambiguous outcome is that with the additions of defender Konsa and midfielder Guimarães, the Premier League champions have strengthened a core that was already exceptionally strong; Arteta might have to call on his man-management skills to keep certain players happy.

Konsa adds depth to an already impressive defense in the wake of an injury to William Saliba, while Guimarães does the same to central midfield as Zubimendi and Merino struggled for form and fitness respectively.

In attack, the club went through a mini-revamp. Four first-team players left -- Gabriel Jesus (Barcelona), Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Gabriel Martinelli (Al Hilal) and Ethan Nwaneri (loan, Dortmund) -- while only one, Tzolis, arrived. The Greece international has made an encouraging start and gives Arteta a different option from the left, with a superb right foot and set-piece expertise, and while Eze and Madueke can deputize there, Tzolis is the only specialist in the role. Using either of the former two on the left may also reduce the cover available elsewhere, particularly for the injury-prone Ødegaard. In that sense, the right side of the attack looks more complete than the left, with Saka backed up by Madueke and emerging teenager Dowman.

At center forward, it is not so much a case of accommodating new arrivals as managing the pecking order. One year after joining, Gyökeres has gone from being the No. 9 starter Arsenal bought him for to fighting to regain his place and looking to convince everyone he's not an expensive flop. Havertz's form in the opening weeks has made the striking selection easy for Arteta, and even if having two senior center forwards of contrasting profiles is a luxury, the question here is how long the Sweden star will tolerate his bit-part status.

CHELSEA

Goalkeeper: Emiliano Martínez, Mike Penders, Gabriel Slonina

Right back: Reece James, Malo Gusto, Marco Palestra

Left back: Jorrel Hato, Pep Chavarría

Center back: Wesley Fofana, Maxence Lacroix, Levi Colwill, Josh Acheampong, Aaron Anselmino

Central midfield: Moisés Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, Cole Palmer, Jordan Henderson, Valentín Barco

Attacking midfield/Forward: Morgan Rogers, Estêvão, Pedro Neto, Geovany Quenda, Jamie Gittens

Striker: João Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha, Danny Welbeck

FIRST XI (3-4-2-1)

Martinez

Fofana, Lacroix, Colwill

Neto, Caicedo, James, Hato

Palmer, Rogers

João Pedro

SECOND XI (3-4-2-1)

Penders

Gusto, Anselmino, Acheamapong

Palestra, Lavia, Barco, Chavarria

Estevao, Gittens

Emegha

EXTRAS: Slonina, Quenda, Henderson, Welbeck

As in previous years, Chelsea are still difficult to assess due to the sheer volume of their transfer activity, with 13 arrivals and 39 exits (22 on loan). Continuity is still missing and players have come and gone at such a rate that relatively few have been given the time to settle properly, establish a clear role or develop within a stable structure. True to this blueprint -- whether forced or by design -- this summer brought another considerable turnover, though there was at least one notable shift in approach.

The arrivals of 36-year-old midfielder Henderson and 35-year-old striker Welbeck represented a tweak to Chelsea's recent transfer policy. After several windows dominated by younger players, both England internationals brought the type of experience and dressing room presence many felt the Blues' squad had been lacking. Aston Villa goalkeeper Martinez, 34, also brought experience and a quality upgrade between the posts.

But as much as it this newly-found pragmatism was needed, the early signs this season suggest that Chelsea are still in locked in what seems to be a perpetual rebuild under new coach Xabi Alonso.

At the back there are plenty of options, with full backs able to switch sides or even slot into Alonso's preferred back three. Yet the squad numbers haven't quite turned into solidity. While Chelsea can field several convincing-looking defensive line-ups on paper -- with Fofana and James the rare survivors from the Clearlake era -- the unit still lacks the cohesion (especially since Alonso brought in another new formation) of the Premier League's strongest sides. For all its talent and depth, the overriding impression is still one of a defense searching for stability rather than one that has reached its final shape.

Central midfield looks more vulnerable. The departures of Enzo Fernández (to Man City) and Andrey Santos (to Man United) have diminished the options around Caicedo, whose defensive influence remains difficult to replace. Lavia's continued fitness issues make that dependence even more precarious, while Henderson, for all his experience, is not the force he once was.

While there is no shortage of options up front, either, Alonso's requirement of tucking in his wide attackers to allow space in the attacking lanes for his wing backs presents some tactical challenges. Palmer and Rogers are world-class players, but the question is whether the 3-4-2-1 formation allows enough width for a pair that tends to prefer to start their diagonal movement close to the touchline. That said, there's plenty of quality in depth -- Quenda, Neto, Estevao -- to support Joao Pedro up front, though the challenge is finding the right formula.

LIVERPOOL

Goalkeeper: Alisson Becker, Giorgi Mamardashvili, Freddie Woodman

Right back: Ronald Araújo, Jeremie Frimpong, Conor Bradley

Left back: Milos Kerkez, Kostas Tsimikas

Center back: Virgil van Dijk, Jérémy Jacquet, Joe Gomez, Giovanni Leoni

Central midfield: Dominik Szoboszlai, Ryan Gravenberch, Florian Wirtz, Alexis Mac Allister, Trey Nyoni, Wataru Endo, James McConnell

Attacking midfield/Forward: Bradley Barcola, Cody Gakpo, Víctor Muñoz, Rio Ngumoha, Federico Chiesa

Striker: Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike, Lewis Koumas

FIRST XI (4-2-3-1)

Alisson

Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez

Szoboszlai, Mac Allister

Barcola, Wirtz, Gakpo

Isak

SECOND XI (4-2-3-1)

Mamardashvili

Frimpong, Gomez, Leoni, Tsimikas

Gravenberch, Nyoni

Munoz, Chiesa, Ngumoha

Koumas

EXTRAS: Woodman, Endo, McConnell

LONG-TERM INJURIES: Bradley, Ekitike

Liverpool's biggest concern is not necessarily the quality of the squad, but its relative thinness. Just one injury in several spots could quickly cause a domino effect that affects the whole team's structure, and that begins in goal, especially when it comes to playing out from the back. Alisson is still one of the outstanding ball-playing goalkeepers in Europe, but while Mamardashvili was recruited as his long-term successor, he has yet to look like a truly convincing alternative. For a club competing on several fronts, that drop in quality from first to second choice might eventually present some unwanted issues.

In defense, signing another center back wouldn't have gone amiss, particularly given Van Dijk's age (35) and Joe Gomez's injury history. That said, €70 million summer arrival Jacquet and Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo have alleviated those concerns to a certain degree. Both players have looked promising already and appear to be credible starting options. Iraola doesn't seem to rate Frimpong's defending and while Araujo deals well with the right-back role defensively, questions remain over whether he offers enough forward thrust while Bradley is still recovering from a serious knee injury.

Though the midfield is strong, another combative ball winner would have been more than welcome. Szoboszlai can operate deeper without weakening Liverpool, or at right back, but that versatility -- albeit useful -- poses another question: if Wirtz continues to struggle for consistency, who fills the No. 10 role when Szoboszlai is required further back? One positive consequence of the relatively small midfield selection is that the highly rated teenager Nyoni should see playing time.

Up front, France winger Barcola was a particularly useful attacking addition from PSG. His ability to operate from either flank or through the middle gives Iraola some peace of mind and reduces the dependence on any one wide player. The greater worry is at center forward, with Ekitike still some way from returning following his Achilles injury. Consequently, a serious workload will be placed on Isak as Liverpool's only established senior No. 9; signing another specialist striker would have made the squad more robust.

MANCHESTER CITY

Goalkeepers: Gianluigi Donnarumma, Gerónimo Rulli, Marcus Bettinelli

Right back: Matheus Nunes, Rico Lewis

Left back: Nico O'Reilly, Rayan Aït-Nouri

Center back: Rúben Dias, Marc Guéhi, Joško Gvardiol, Abdukodir Khusanov, Vitor Reis

Attacking midfield/Forward: Rayan Cherki, Phil Foden, Jérémy Doku, Iliman Ndiaye, Antoine Semenyo, Allan, Ryan McAidoo

Striker: Erling Haaland, Floyd Samba

FIRST XI (4-2-3-1)

EXTRAS: Bettinelli, McAidoo

City's squad has undergone a remarkable overhaul over the past years (for which they may pay the price). Kevin De Bruyne and Rodri are two world-class names to have departed, while only Haaland and Dias remain from the starting XI that won the Champions League final in 2022-23. This year, the team also had to contend with the exit of legendary manager Pep Guardiola. However, the early signs suggest that, under Guardiola's former assistant Enzo Maresca, the squad is younger, more athletic and, importantly, more balanced.

Center back is the one defensive area that looks slightly light. While Dias and Guéhi have quickly developed into a strong first-choice partnership, Khusanov -- who has already shown he can deputize without a huge drop on quality -- is the only back-up and another out-and-out center back may have been needed. Sure, Gvardiol can also move inside from left back when required, but the four major competitions (plus internationals) will put a lot of strain on defensive depth.

This summer the City midfield changed almost beyond recognition. With influential Rodri gone, City moved toward a double pivot, with Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson already looking a good match. The Fernandez provides ball-carrying and playmaking, while Anderson brings mobility, aggression, stamina and an ability to connect the play. The 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi presents another exciting option, but further up the pitch City have fewer of the floating, interchangeable attacking midfielders that became such a feature of the Guardiola years. For that reason, Maresca will probably have to get double figures in assists and goals from Phil Foden and Rayan Cherki to sustain a title challenge.

Up front, Haaland is the obvious reference point, and City's decision not to recruit an orthodox back-up striker does seem deliberate. But it's tricky to see what Maresca would do should the Norway international be absent for a lengthy spell.

MANCHESTER UNITED

Goalkeepers: Senne Lammens, Karl Darlow, Tom Heaton

Right back: Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui

Left back: Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu, Harry Amass

Center back: Lisandro Martínez, Harry Maguire, Matthijs de Ligt, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven

Central midfield: Kobbie Mainoo, Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, Manuel Ugarte, Tyler Fletcher

Attacking midfield/Forward: Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Marcus Rashford, Amad Diallo, Shea Lacey, Mason Mount

Striker: Benjamin Sesko, Matheus Cunha, Joshua Zirkzee

FIRST XI (4-2-3-1)

Lammens

Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw

Mainoo, Baleba

Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford

Cunha

SECOND XI (4-2-3-1)

Darlow

Mazraoui, Yoro, De Ligt, Dorgu

Tielemans, Santos

Diallo, Mount, Lacey

Sesko

EXTRAS: Heaton, Heaven, Fletcher, Zirkzee

LONG-TERM INJURY: Ugarte

While United's squad depth looks healthier than it has for some time, particularly in midfield and attack, there are still clear areas of vulnerability. In addition to just having one quality goalkeeper, the defense is arguably where the squad looks at its frailest. At center back, the club could do with another reliable, senior figure (with pace), and the lingering doubts over the full backs -- which also extends to the first-choice pair Dalot and Shaw -- are still there.

Indeed, those defensive uncertainties expose wider tactical problems as United are still vulnerable to transitions due to a lack of recovery speed in the center. The absence of a quality ball-playing center back (at least while the injury-prone De Ligt is out) also limits the build-up from deep.

On the positive side, the clearest improvement has come in central midfield. Baleba, Santos and Tielemans give new boss Michael Carrick several strong alternatives behind Fernandes. Baleba should make sure the club's disappointing sprint numbers increase, in addition to providing ball-winning and connection work between defense and attack; similarly, Santos injects industry, technical quality and runs into the box, while Tielemans was a smart addition and should see to improved creativity and goal threat from midfield. With young Mainoo as another option, this means four credible names to compete for two spots.

Still, as much as that midfield depth is important, United are still heavily dependent on Fernandes for the attacking role in midfield and there's no like-for-like replacement that comes anywhere near his attacking influence (especially since Mount has never really got going). The emergence of homegrown players such as Lacey and Fletcher is another positive for a side that haven't been spoiled for emerging academy graduates over the past few seasons.

Despite no new summer additions, the attack does look fairly balanced. There is explosive pace and presence in the box via Mbeumo and other diverse technical profiles -- Cunha is technically gifted; Sesko is a powerful, traditional No. 9 -- allow greater rotation and tactical flexibility. A resurgent Rashford would also prove a huge plus after he returned from loan at Barcelona.

The snag here, however, is mostly to do with variable performances and the fact several players signed over recent windows are yet to reproduce the level they showed at their previous clubs. Though hardly considered title contenders, despite finishing third last year, United do have a marginally deeper squad than in recent seasons and just need to show a better way to deal with opponents who sit behind the ball.

TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR

Goalkeepers: Antonín Kinsky, Martin Dúbravka, Brandon Austin

Right-back: Pedro Porro, Archie Gray

Left-back: Andy Robertson, Destiny Udogie

Centre-back: Micky van de Ven, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Tosin Adarabioyo, Ben Davies

Central midfield: Sandro Tonali, Rodrigo Bentancur, Mateus Fernandes, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Dejan Kulusevski

Attacking midfield/Forward: Sávio, Mathys Tel, Mohammed Kudus, Mykhailo Mudryk, Wilson Odobert, James Maddison, Xavi Simons

Striker: Dominic Solanke, Omar Marmoush

FIRST XI (4-2-3-1)

Kinsky

Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson

Tonali, Fernandes

Kudus, Maddison, Savio

Marmoush

SECOND XI (4-2-3-1)
Dubravka

Gray, Adarabioyo, Senesi, Udogie

Bentancur, Bergvall

Kulusevski, Gallagher, Tel

Solanke

Having spent more than £300 million over the summer after their flirtation with relegation last season, Tottenham have unquestionably refreshed the squad, though sit bottom of the league after five league games with no wins, and only two goals scored.

The defense had a proper makeover with Senesi, Van Hecke and Adarabioyo joining a squad that already contained Van de Ven and only lost Djed Spence, Cristian Romero and Luka Vuskovic. In terms of numbers and individual quality, the center back position now looks stronger and there is reason to expect the defensive record to improve. However, the issue at hand is more of a structural nature, with the center backs having to adjust to new coach Roberto De Zerbi's demanding, high-risk style of defending (on and off the ball).

While the midfield depth should be fine with Tonali and Fernandes, neither have hit the ground running despite being signed for a combined fee of £185 million. Tonali, at times looking slow and static, is still adapting and Fernandes has been tried in different roles without establishing a clear tactical remit. Nonetheless, the other options are more than decent and the return to full fitness of Maddison and Simons should improve the creativity between the lines. Meanwhile, if he returns to his pre-injury self, Kulusevski will provide additional threat either centrally or from wide areas.

The attack raises more questions, however, as Tottenham have drawn a blank in all but one league game so far. Marmoush has yet to fire, and for all his quality, there is the same positional puzzle that followed him at Manchester City: Is he ultimately a center forward, a No. 10 or a left winger? Sure, De Zerbi himself has already hinted that he can fill all those roles, but is he likely to be prolific in any of them? Dominic Solanke is available as a more orthodox No. 9, but the evidence so far hardly points to him suddenly transforming the Tottenham front line. Furthermore, Mathys Tel does not yet look a 15-goal-plus Premier League striker either.

Given the debacle around the future of Richarlison -- who fell out with De Zerbi and was left out of the Premier League squad but didn't move clubs -- signing another center forward would have made sense. There are also plenty of wide options, but Savio (£75 million, Manchester City) and Mykhailo Mudryk (loan, Chelsea) -- who De Zerbi has long rated highly -- have tended to come up with their best football in flashes rather than consistently (and Mudryk had not played a competitive game since November 2024, having been suspended for four years after failing a drug test.)

On paper, Spurs possess an intriguing attacking mixture of established internationals and high-end prospects, but the challenge for De Zerbi is finding a structure that allows the players to flourish at the same time and build some cohesion.

stories.headline: AFL overreactions: Brisbane can't win the 2027 flag without Chris Fagan and Lachie Neale
stories.summary: The season might be over, but there is still plenty to talk about -- particularly at the Lions. Chris Fagan is gone, Lachie Neale is off to Collingwood, and suddenly Brisbane's future looks very different.
stories.body:
The season might be over, but there is still plenty to talk about -- particularly at the Lions. Chris Fagan is gone, Lachie Neale is off to Collingwood, and suddenly Brisbane's future looks very different.

Let's get to this week's overreactions column, where we judge the biggest takeaway as legitimate or irrational.

Brisbane can't win the 2027 premiership without Chris Fagan and Lachie Neale
Beloved Lions coach Chris Fagan revealed to his playing group on Thursday morning that he would be departing the club and drawing the curtain on one of the greatest coaching decades in football history.

Fagan coached Brisbane for 10 seasons and on Saturday afternoon became just the sixth man to lead a team to a premiership three-peat.

The 65-year-old joins dual Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale as off-season Lions departures. Earlier in the week, Neale informed the club of his intent to sign with Collingwood as an unrestricted free agent.

Verdict: Overreaction

The losses of Fagan and Neale are obviously immense, and one could argue they were the two most critical pieces to Brisbane's dynastic run. But does anyone really believe this club is now set to nosedive? I didn't think so.

Let's start with Fagan. He leaves behind a Hall of Fame-worthy legacy and some mammoth shoes to fill. But there may not be a club more prepared to fill them than the Lions. Football boss Danny Daly, who has been involved in the AFL for 26 years, is someone that's been both waiting in the wings and long touted as a future senior coach. Should he get the nod, there are many at clubland who believe he can carry on what Fagan has built.

And then there's Neale. Like Fagan, he departs with an all-time resume, but a reminder, he's 33 years of age and probably now behind Will Ashcroft in the club's midfield pecking order. Neale's void isn't one that must be plugged, necessarily, rather it will provide opportunity for others to step up and take on greater responsibility.

Brisbane has already shown it knows how to evolve. This club didn't win three premierships by relying solely on Fagan and Neale. Luke Hodge, for example, helped steady the ship in the early years of Fagan's tenure before the Lions' flag run began. And since then the club has continued to build a deep, talented list.

The Lions might be the second-oldest team on paper, but that's selling short their future. Harris Andrews, Josh Dunkley, Tom Doedee, Jarrod Berry, and Hugh McCluggage are all still on the right side of 30, while Kai Lohmann, Darcy Wilmot, Jaspa Fletcher, Will Ashcroft, Logan Morris, Ty Gallop, Levi Ashcroft, and Daniel Annable are all aged under 24.

The Fagan era is over. The Neale era is over. But that doesn't necessarily mean the Lions' era is, too.

-- Jake Michaels

stories.headline: Padres silence Cubs' bats again, finish off 2-game wild-card sweep
stories.summary: Five Padres pitchers combined on a five-hitter and Gavin Sheets hit a pinch-hit two-run homer, as San Diego swept the Cubs out of the NL Wild Card Series with a 4-1 win.
stories.body:
SAN DIEGO -- Pinch hitter Gavin Sheets blasted a two-run homer, five Padres pitchers combined on a five-hitter, and San Diego swept the Chicago Cubs out of the National League Wild Card Series with a 4-1 victory in Game 2 on Wednesday night.

Xander Bogaerts drove in the first run for the surging Padres, who followed up their 8-0 victory in Tuesday's opener with another dominant mound performance. The Cubs led the majors in runs and the NL in homers this year, but they managed just eight hits -- seven singles -- over 18 innings against San Diego's inspired staff.

Ethan Salas drove in a run while becoming the youngest player to catch a postseason game in major league history for the Padres, whose 19-3 surge since Sept. 5 has them looking like a threat in the NL.

One year after the Cubs eliminated the Padres in three tough wild-card games at Wrigley Field, the Padres reversed the result in two romps before frenzied sellout crowds at Petco Park.

With their fifth playoff series victory in the past seven years, the Padres advanced to face the MLB-best Milwaukee Brewers in an NL division series this weekend.

Game 1 of the division series is Saturday in Milwaukee. The Padres took four of six from the Brewers this season, even sweeping a three-game series at Petco Park in August.
